A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the N/S abundance ratio is lower in the inner Galaxy than in the solar neighborhood, while the N/H and O/H ratios are similar to solar neighborhood values.
the N/H and N/S ratios appear to be smaller than previously estimated, but the N/O ratio remains as high as previously estimated.
the S/H, S/O, S/N, and N/O ratios in the inner Galaxy are similar to those of the local interstellar medium, but the Ne/O ratio is higher.
The main takeaway from our work is that
abundance analyses in H II regions must consider density variations and that the N/O abundance ratios in inner Galaxy H II region may be higher than in the outer Galaxy.

the S/H and O/H abundance ratios, and hence the N/O ratio, in the inner Galaxy are consistent with those found in the outer Galaxy, but with large uncertainties, particularly for the oxygen abundance.
the elemental abundances in the inner Galaxy are similar to those in the solar neighborhood, but with a higher N/O ratio, which may be related to the lower oxygen abundance found in the outer Galaxy.
